question: What topics are established in the twenty-eighth chapter on occasional rites?
premises: The twenty-eighth chapter is called the revelation of occasional rites.
It sets forth the division of the qualified self.
It also sets forth the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
inference: The twenty-eighth chapter combines classification of practitioners with the ordered lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
uncertainties: The exact criteria for the division of the qualified self are not given here.
plain_english: In the twenty-eighth chapter, called the revelation of occasional rites, are established the division of the qualified practitioner and the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
